Landing.heroBody: Smooth wallet payments for stores. The merchant shows a QR with the amount baked in, and the customer just scans and signs. Cross-chain USDC payments arrive automatically too.

Landing.featuresSubtitle: No sign-up, no custody. A payment experience that needs nothing more than a wallet.
Landing.featuresGaslessBody: When the merchant picks gasless mode while building the QR, customers can pay with just JPYC / USDC — no POL or ETH needed. For JPYC, OpenPay bears the network fee in full and collects nothing from the customer or merchant. For USDC, the customer pays gas in USDC via the paymaster (OpenPay collects 0). For cross-chain payments from a different source chain, the source chain's network fee is still paid by the customer.
Landing.featuresMultichainBody: Receive JPYC on Polygon / Kaia, USDC on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism / Polygon / Ethereum / Avalanche. Circle CCTP V2 handles cross-chain USDC payments automatically.
Landing.featuresNoncustodyBody: Funds flow straight to the merchant's wallet — OpenPay never holds your balance. No server-side ledger means no withdrawal approvals.

Landing.faqA1: In gasless mode, customers don't need POL or ETH — they pay with just their JPYC or USDC balance (that's what "gasless" means here). For JPYC payments, OpenPay bears the gas in full and collects no equivalent from customers or merchants; the full payment amount reaches the merchant's wallet (the customer simply signs the transfer in JPYC). For USDC payments, the customer pays gas in USDC to the paymaster, so OpenPay does not collect a gas-equivalent.
Landing.faqQ2: Can I receive both JPYC and USDC?
Landing.faqA2: Yes. JPYC is a good fit when you want JPY-denominated receipts; USDC is better for Web3-savvy or international customers. JPYC (JPY-pegged) is supported on Polygon and Kaia; USDC on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism / Polygon / Ethereum / Avalanche. Pick the chain in the QR builder. If the customer holds the token on a different chain, Circle CCTP V2 settles cross-chain automatically.
Landing.faqQ3: What if the customer has no wallet?
Landing.faqA3: Direct them to a browser wallet (MetaMask, Rabby, etc.) or a mobile wallet (MetaMask Mobile / Rainbow / Coinbase Wallet). OpenPay auto-detects multiple wallets via EIP-6963.
Landing.faqQ4: How do I convert JPYC / USDC to JPY?
Landing.faqA4: JPYC redeems 1:1 at <jpycEx>JPYC EX</jpycEx>. USDC can be sold via SBI VC Trade and other Japanese exchanges. The bottom of the <create>Receive</create> page lists exchange links per token.
Landing.faqA5: History is kept only in your browser's LocalStorage — never sent to OpenPay servers. You can export to CSV from the history page. Transaction hashes are recorded so you can verify on Etherscan / Polygonscan.
Landing.faqA6: The OpenPay monthly usage fee is calculated based on 1% of the amount you receive via JPYC gasless payments (where the Company sponsors the gas) — from the July 2026 usage period; billed in arrears the following month or later; use through the June 2026 usage period is free. The fee is billed monthly rather than deducted from each transaction, and the price of goods is sent directly to the merchant's wallet. Paths where the customer pays gas themselves (e.g. USDC) are not in scope. See the Terms of Service and the Specified Commercial Transactions Act disclosure for details.
Landing.trustBody: OpenPay is built on a non-custodial design (funds are never held by OpenPay) and open-source stablecoin payment technology. All source code is MIT-licensed and public on GitHub — anyone can verify how the payment flow works.
Landing.trustTechStack: Tech stack: EIP-3009 signature relay (self-hosted relayer / Gelato fallback — JPYC gasless) / Circle Paymaster (USDC gasless — gas paid in USDC) / Circle CCTP V2 & Gateway (USDC cross-chain) / ERC-4337 (account abstraction) / ERC-7702 (EOA → smart account delegation) / Pimlico bundler/paymaster (fallback) / viem / wagmi / permissionless.js / Next.js
Landing.supportBody: The OpenPay monthly usage fee is calculated based on 1% of the amount you receive via JPYC gasless payments (where the Company sponsors the gas) — from the July 2026 usage period; billed in arrears; use through the June 2026 usage period is free. The fee is billed monthly rather than deducted from each transaction, and the price of goods is sent directly to the merchant's wallet.
Landing.supportTipRequest: If you'd like to help keep OpenPay running, a tip is hugely appreciated. You can support us from the buttons below (also handy for a quick try).
Landing.benefitsSubtitle: Real value for merchants, simplicity for customers.
Landing.benefitsFeeBody: OpenPay's monthly usage fee, calculated based on 1% of the amount you receive via JPYC gasless payments (from the July 2026 usage period; billed in arrears). That's lower than credit cards (~3%) or typical QR payment services (1.5–3.25%).
Landing.benefitsCostBody: No POS terminal, no contracts, no upfront fees. Just one wallet address — go from start to a printed QR the same day.
Landing.benefitsSettlementBody: Sales land in the merchant wallet the moment the on-chain transaction confirms. No month-end closing, no 2–3 business day waits (non-custodial: OpenPay never holds funds).
Landing.benefitsNoSignupBody: Customers pay with just a wallet — no address, phone or email registration required. No KYC either.
Landing.benefitsWhyLead: Wallet transfers are handy for people who can already send crypto, but they fall short as store payments: you type the recipient and amount by hand, you can pick the wrong chain or token, the store can't easily confirm what a payment is for, and you need a separate token for gas. OpenPay is an open-source payment tool that removes the friction of using wallet transfers at the point of sale.
Landing.benefitsWhyPoint1Body: The store bakes the payment conditions into a QR up front, and the customer just scans it. No hand-typing the recipient, amount, chain or token — so the slip-ups that plague raw wallet transfers go away.
Landing.benefitsWhyPoint2Body: Set a preset or any billed amount and present a clear "pay this amount" QR. Customers don't enter the amount themselves, which makes it practical at a counter or an event.

gasHint.title: When you have no gas (POL / ETH) to send tokens to an exchange
gasHint.body: Sending received JPYC / USDC to an exchange requires a small amount of native gas on each chain (POL on Polygon, ETH on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism). With MetaMask's Swap (Gas Station) feature, you can swap on Polygon / Base / Arbitrum without holding any POL or ETH — the gas fee is paid out of your JPYC or USDC. On chains where Gas Station is not available (e.g. Optimism), a small amount of ETH is required separately to initiate the swap.
gasHint.disclaimer: Note: Availability, supported chains, and success of MetaMask features depend on MetaMask itself; OpenPay is not involved. Network congestion or unsupported token routes on any chain may cause the swap to fail.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: {company} (the "Company") establishes this Privacy Policy (the "Policy") regarding the handling of personal information in connection with the blockchain payment service "{service}" (the "Service"), in compliance with the Act on the Protection of Personal Information of Japan (the "APPI") and related laws.

section1.title: 1. Information We Collect
section1.body: We collect the following information in connection with the Service: (1) blockchain wallet addresses that the Company observes when users connect their wallet to the Service; (2) server log information including browser information, IP address, referrer, access timestamps, and page navigation; (3) anonymized statistics collected by Vercel Analytics, such as page views, visitor country/region, and device type; (4) email address and inquiry content when users contact us; (5) on-chain transaction information generated or referenced through the Service (such as transaction hash, sender wallet address, recipient wallet address, supported token, supported chain, transfer amount, OpenPay usage fee, payment mode, and payment status); (6) if the user grants camera permission on pages such as /scan for QR code reading, the camera video frames and the decoded QR string. Some of this information is publicly recorded on the blockchain and may not be deletable or hideable by the Company. To provide the Service's functionality, the Company may store in the user's browser local storage settings related to display and payments, transaction history, payment receipts, wallet connection state, and similar data. Such data is used within the client (the user's device) and is not transmitted to the Company's servers, nor used for cross-site behavioral tracking or advertising. The Company does not use tracking or advertising cookies. For features that involve sign-in (where used), the Company may use session cookies necessary to provide those features. The Company does not collect special-care-required personal information (such as race, creed, social status, medical history, or criminal record). The Company also does not carry out automated decision-making (including profiling) regarding users. Users may delete this client-side data at any time by clearing their browser cache or storage, or by using the deletion features within the Service (such as deleting payment receipts or transaction history).

section2.title: 2. Purposes of Use
section2.body: We use collected information for: (1) providing, operating, maintaining, and improving the Service; (2) responding to user inquiries; (3) statistical analysis and Service improvement; (4) detecting and preventing fraud, abuse, and unauthorized access; (5) responding to legal obligations; (6) other purposes ancillary to the above; (7) confirming payment status, calculating the OpenPay usage fee, executing gas sponsorship in Gasless Payment mode, detecting fraud, and handling inquiries and incident investigations; (8) camera frames on pages such as /scan are processed entirely within the user's browser to decode the QR code and are never transmitted to the Company's servers or any external destination, nor are they stored. Of the decoded results, only the OpenPay payment URL category that the Service recognizes (pay / tip / checkout / external / eip681 / unknown) is sent to Sentry as an error-observation breadcrumb; the raw QR string and the user's wallet address are not sent to Sentry. The Company configures its error monitoring not to send personally identifying information, and if unnecessary personal data is nonetheless included in an error log, it will take reasonable measures such as deletion or masking.

section3.title: 3. Sharing with Third Parties and Service Providers
section3.body: We do not share personal information with third parties without user consent or where required by law. However, we engage the following service providers to operate the Service, all of which we supervise as required by the APPI: - Vercel Inc. (United States): hosting, CDN, analytics. - Pimlico Labs Inc. (United States): ERC-4337 bundler and paymaster service. - Circle Internet Financial, Inc. (United States): Circle Paymaster (ERC-4337 paymaster) service for USDC gasless payments. The customer pays the gas-equivalent amount in USDC to that paymaster; the Company does not collect or receive that fee. - Alchemy Insights Inc. (United States): blockchain RPC. Because these providers are located in the United States, personal information may be transferred to a third party located in a foreign country (APPI Article 28). We have data protection agreements in place with these providers and have implemented measures to protect users' rights and interests.

section2.body: Transactions executed through the Service (transfers, token exchanges, and other on-chain actions) cannot be cancelled, refunded, or modified due to the technical nature of blockchain. section3.body: JPYC is an electronic payment instrument (a JPY-denominated stablecoin) issued by JPYC Inc. as a funds transfer service provider registered under Japan's Payment Services Act; USDC is a stablecoin issued by Circle Internet Financial, Inc. Each Supported Token is issued and operated by a third-party issuer independent of the Company. Each token does not guarantee that it will maintain its peg (e.g., 1 JPYC = 1 JPY, 1 USDC = 1 USD); its value may fluctuate or deviate from that peg (de-peg) depending on the issuer's situation and market conditions.

section4.title: 4. Network Fee Volatility
section4.body: Network fees (gas) are required for on-chain transactions and vary significantly with network congestion, underlying asset prices, and other factors outside the Company's control. In Gasless Payment mode, the gas estimates shown by the Service are best-effort estimates at the time of display and actual amounts may exceed them. In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Customer pays the Network Fee from their own wallet according to the estimate displayed by the wallet application. The Company is not liable for losses arising from gas spikes or volatility.

section5.title: 5. Third-Party Service Outages
section5.body: The Service depends on third-party providers including Pimlico (ERC-4337 bundler/paymaster), Alchemy (RPC), Vercel (hosting), wallet applications, and the blockchain networks themselves. The Company is not liable when the Service becomes wholly or partially unavailable, or when users incur losses, due to outages, suspensions, specification changes, deprecation, or performance degradation of these third-party services.

section6.title: 6. Changes in Laws and Regulatory Risk
section6.body: Crypto and blockchain-related laws and regulations may change in Japan and other jurisdictions. The Company is not liable for losses arising when the Service becomes wholly or partially unavailable due to changes in law, regulatory guidance, or compliance measures. Users are responsible for complying with laws applicable to their place of residence and use, and for confirming that their transactions through the Service are not illegal.

section7.title: 7. OpenPay Usage Fee and Gas Sponsorship
section7.body: The OpenPay usage fee is a monthly usage fee borne by Merchants who use JPYC gasless payments, as consideration for use of the Service—including payment processing, merchant QR code generation, the checkout UI, supported wallet integration, gas sponsorship and payment relay for JPYC gasless payments, and operation and maintenance of the Service. The OpenPay usage fee accrues from the July 2026 usage period onward, is calculated based on 1% of the amount received by the Merchant via JPYC gasless payments in the relevant month, and is billed in arrears in the following month or later (use through the June 2026 usage period is free; the fee is triggered by JPYC gasless usage, and paths where the Customer pays gas themselves—e.g. USDC via the ERC20 Paymaster—are not in scope). The OpenPay usage fee is billed monthly rather than deducted from each transaction; the price of goods and similar amounts continues to be transferred in full directly to the Merchant's wallet. In Gasless Payment paths where the Company sponsors gas (e.g. JPYC payments), the Company bears that Network Fee in full and does not collect a gas-equivalent amount from the user for the purpose of recovery (the OpenPay usage fee is not linked to the actual gas amount). Transfers finalized on-chain cannot, by their technical nature, in principle be cancelled, refunded, or modified. In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Company does not handle the Network Fee in any way; the Customer pays it from their own wallet. If the OpenPay usage fee is unpaid, the Company may suspend gasless payment relay for that Merchant, but the act of receiving a payment itself and the use of Standard Payment (with Gas) mode remain available. If the rate, calculation method, or billing method of the OpenPay usage fee is changed, the Company will give prior notice.

section8.title: 8. Use during the Alpha Phase
section8.body: The Service is currently in alpha. Unexpected defects, display errors, transfer failures, wallet connection issues, specification changes to supported chains and tokens, third-party infrastructure outages, and similar events may occur. Before using the Service for real transactions, you must send small test amounts and confirm the destination wallet, amount, supported token, supported chain, payment mode, displayed fees, and the payment-completion flow.

price.label: Consideration for the Service (OpenPay Usage Fee)
price.value: The OpenPay usage fee is a monthly usage fee borne by Merchants who use JPYC gasless payments (where the Company sponsors the gas). It accrues from the July 2026 usage period onward, is calculated based on 1% of the amount received by the Merchant via JPYC gasless payments in the relevant month, and is billed in arrears in the following month or later (use through the June 2026 usage period is free (0%); the fee is triggered by JPYC gasless usage, and paths where the Customer pays gas themselves—e.g. USDC via the ERC20 Paymaster—are not in scope). The OpenPay usage fee is billed monthly rather than deducted from each transaction, as a monthly consideration for using the Service (payment processing, merchant QR code generation, the checkout UI, supported wallet integration, gas sponsorship and payment relay, and operation and maintenance). The price of goods and similar amounts continues to be transferred in full directly to the Merchant's wallet (the Company does not receive, hold, or settle sales), and the OpenPay usage fee is transferred separately from the Merchant's wallet to a wallet designated by the Company. Costs per payment mode are as follows. (1) Gasless Payment mode: in paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee (gas) (e.g. JPYC payments), the Company bears that Network Fee in full and does not collect a gas-equivalent amount from the user for the purpose of recovery (the OpenPay usage fee is not linked to the actual gas amount). The price of goods and similar amounts are transferred in full directly to the Merchant's wallet. In paths where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and the Company does not collect it. (2) Standard Payment (with Gas) mode: the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee; the Customer pays it in the native token from their own wallet. No OpenPay usage fee arises for the act of receiving a payment itself or for the use of Standard Payment (with Gas) mode.

additionalFees.label: Additional Costs
additionalFees.value: (1) Network fees (gas): fees required for confirming transactions on the blockchain. In Gasless Payment mode, the user may be able to pay without separately holding native tokens such as POL or ETH. Specifically, in paths where the Company sponsors gas (e.g. JPYC payments) the Company bears that gas in full and does not collect any equivalent from the user. In paths where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), the Customer pays the gas to the Paymaster provider in USDC or similar, and the Company does not collect it. In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Customer pays the Network Fee in the native token (POL, ETH, etc.) from their own wallet. (2) Wallet application fees: governed by the terms of the wallet application chosen by the user. (3) Communication costs: internet connection charges and communication costs required to use the Service are borne by the user.

serviceStartTiming.label: Service Provision Timing
serviceStartTiming.value: Service to a Merchant begins when the Merchant connects a wallet and generates a QR code. Payment between Customer and Merchant is completed when the Customer scans the QR, approves the transfer in their wallet, and the transaction is finalized on-chain.

paymentTiming.label: Payment Timing and Method
paymentTiming.value: Payments through the Service are transferred on-chain directly from the Customer's wallet to the Merchant's designated wallet at the time each transaction is executed. In Gasless Payment where the Company sponsors gas (e.g. JPYC payments), the Company bears that Network Fee in full and no transfer is made to a wallet designated by the Company (and where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token, e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC, that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and no transfer is made to a wallet designated by the Company). The OpenPay usage fee (a monthly usage fee borne by Merchants who use JPYC gasless payments; accruing from the July 2026 usage period; calculated based on 1% of the amount received via JPYC gasless payments in the month) is billed in arrears in the following month or later and is paid by on-chain transfer of a Supported Token (such as JPYC) from the Merchant's wallet to a wallet designated by the Company (use through the June 2026 usage period is free). If the OpenPay usage fee is unpaid, the Company may suspend gasless payment relay for that Merchant (the act of receiving a payment itself and Standard Payment (with Gas) mode remain available). The Company does not receive, hold, manage, or later settle the price of goods, service fees, or other sales proceeds payable to Merchants. The Company does not issue separate invoices, hold funds in escrow, operate a prepaid charge system, or settle merchant sales. The only payment method for the Service is on-chain transfer of Supported Tokens (such as JPYC / USDC); credit cards, bank transfers, cash, and other payment methods are not supported.

returnPolicy.label: Refunds and Cancellations
returnPolicy.value: Due to the technical nature of blockchain, finalized transfers (including transfers of the price of goods) cannot, in principle, be cancelled, refunded, or modified. The OpenPay usage fee is consideration for use of the Service, including payment processing, gas sponsorship and payment relay in Gasless Payment mode, and mitigation of network-fee volatility risk, and is, in principle, non-refundable after payment (use through the June 2026 usage period is free, and from the July 2026 usage period a monthly usage fee calculated based on 1% of the amount received via JPYC gasless payments in the month applies). In Gasless Payment where the Company sponsors gas (e.g. JPYC payments), the Company bears that gas in full and does not collect a gas-equivalent amount from the user for the purpose of recovery, so no refund or difference settlement arises. Before submitting, users must verify the destination address, amount, supported token, supported chain, and payment mode. If the Service is unusable due to a material defect, please contact us by email; we will investigate and respond within a reasonable scope. The Service is an alpha version provided "as is," and the Company does not provide any special warranty (including warranty against defects) for the Service (see the Disclaimer and Terms of Service for details). Furthermore, any dispute concerning defects, non-delivery, quantity discrepancies, or cancellation of goods or services paid for through the Service shall be resolved directly between the merchant and the customer; the Company is not a party to such sales contracts and bears no liability for them.
